learning_outcomes.text: Represent information in a format that can be processed by a computer
Manipulate logical expressions and functions to obtain the most suitable forms for implementation with electronic devices
Translate high-level functional specifications into logical functions
Translate an abstract, moderately complex problem into the formulation of a finite state machine
Synthesize a finite state machine using a combination of basic logic gates and memory registers
Estimate the dynamic performance of a moderately complex system, based on the specifications of its basic logic blocks
Understand and explore the concept of abstraction levels in digital design
Represent moderately complex systems as combinations of simpler subsystems
Understand and use some control and communication protocols between fundamental blocks, and recognize potential issues arising from the dynamic limitations of real components
Acquire the basics of performance optimization through appropriate architectural choices
Understand and identify the potential and limitations of the main types of memory, depending on the application context
Apply priority techniques and communication protocols in managing shared resources
Describe digital systems using a dedicated language
Identify a code formulation that can be synthesized
Organize code for the description of complex systems in hierarchical levels

syllabus_topics: Binary representation of numerical and non-numerical information
Concept of logic operator and logic gate; difference between ideal and real logic gates
Synthesis, transformation, and optimization of logic circuits and standard implementations
Concept of sequential system, state variables, and representation as a combination of a combinational system and memory elements
Knowledge of various latches and registers and their dynamic properties
Main dynamic limitations of a sequential system
Basic computer architecture and understanding of control flow
Fundamental blocks of an ALU and related architectural solutions
Main types of memory and their architectures.
Knowledge of key dynamic limitations and their consequences at the system level
Main techniques for bus access management and input/output protocols
Use of the VHDL language for the representation, logic simulation, and synthesis of digital systems, including complex ones
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)
Use of digital system logic simulation tools through the VHDL language

assessment_methods.method: Written test (exercises involving analysis or synthesis of digital circuits, possibly including hardware description languages)

assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written test with an approximate duration of 3 hours. The assessment is based on the knowledge and understanding of concepts and methodologies, and the ability to apply them to solve specific problems. The evaluation criteria for the written exam will be accuracy and completeness of the answers. The use of any Artificial Intelligence tools during the exam is strictly prohibited.
bibliography: M. Mano, C. R. Kime, T. Martin: Logic and Computer Design Fundamentals, Pearson, 2015.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica (Electronic Engineering), classe L-8 R Ingegneria dell'informazione
